data.content_ref: inline:The isolated artifact 084384ac0b1e depends on SRC_005's claim that independence is a property of the evidential channel, not the engine boundary, but contradicts SRC_005 by insisting that channel-level decorrelation is unobservable in any single run and therefore the principle is unfalsifiable without the very case-level procedures (SRC_002's execution traces, SRC_003's injected-false-claim populations) it was meant to cover. The contradiction is that SRC_005's covering principle subsumes its own evidential basis: if causal decorrelation is the sole criterion, the case-level operations that detect it are treated as mere instances, yet without them the principle has no empirical grip on any concrete run. It is refuted if SRC_005's decorrelation criterion can be operationalized and measured at the single-run level without recourse to the population statistics or execution traces it was designed to subsume, or if the principle is shown to generate no disagreement with the case-level tests it was meant to unify.
